query: Earlier refractory high-entropy alloys illustrate persistent trade-offs: MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW retained good yield strength from 600 to 1600 °C, with MoNbTaVW reaching 842 MPa at 1000 °C, but both had poor room-temperature fracture toughness and high density; HfNbTaTiZr showed room-temperature ductility above 50% and a yield strength of 929 MPa but only 295 MPa at 1000 °C; and as-cast HfMoTaTiZr achieved about 1600 MPa at room temperature and 855 MPa at elevated temperature but retained a density of 10.21 g cm−3. Given the constraint that density must be reduced without sacrificing the strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, what single intervention should be tested? Provide a mechanistic hypothesis, predicted outcomes relative to the as-cast baseline, explicit temperature and loading boundary conditions, supporting evidence from the preceding RHEA results, and a controlled experiment with quantitative rejection criteria that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Reducing the density of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr without sacrificing its strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance can be achieved by introducing a specific amount of aluminum (Al) into the alloy, which forms a dense oxidation film on the surface, thus improving high-temperature oxidation resistance.
generation.intervention: introduction of aluminum (Al) into the alloy
generation.structural_mediator: formation of a dense oxidation film on the surface
generation.predicted_outcome: reduced density without sacrificing strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance
generation.uncertainty: the optimal amount of aluminum (Al) to be introduced and its effect on the mechanical properties of the alloy

falsification_experiment.design: controlled experiment with varying amounts of aluminum (Al) introduction into the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy
measurements: mechanical properties (yield strength, fracture toughness) at room and high temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the introduction of aluminum (Al) does not result in a significant reduction in density without sacrificing strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance, the hypothesis is falsified
